I added the one-line comment to `scripts/check.sh`, directly above the line that sets the variable. Nothing else changed, and I did not commit.

**1. Full `git diff`**
```diff
diff --git a/scripts/check.sh b/scripts/check.sh
index ca11304..1f91457 100755
--- a/scripts/check.sh
+++ b/scripts/check.sh
@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 # Advisory pre-commit check: warns about large staged files.
 set -uo pipefail
 
+# CHECK_LIMIT_KB: size threshold in KB above which a staged file is flagged (default 512).
 limit_kb=${CHECK_LIMIT_KB:-512}
 big=$(git diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
   [ -f "$f" ] || continue
```

**2. Where the default is defined** (line 5 of `scripts/check.sh`, verbatim):
```
limit_kb=${CHECK_LIMIT_KB:-512}
```
The script computes each staged file's size as `wc -c` divided by 1024, so the unit is KB. A file is flagged when `kb -gt "$limit_kb"`, so it must be strictly larger than the limit. That matches the "above which" wording in the comment. The default is not defined anywhere else.

**3. PRECEDENT.md**
There is no `PRECEDENT.md` at the repo root. `scripts/PRECEDENT.md` exists and has one record for `check.sh`:

> ### §check-fails-open — the check never blocks a commit because of its own failure
> - Decision: `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`. Every internal error still ends in `exit 0`; the script only warns.
> - Forbidden: `set -e` or `set -o errexit`, and any exit status other than 0.

It says nothing about comments, the header of `check.sh`, or `CHECK_LIMIT_KB`. Adding a comment doesn't touch `set -uo pipefail` or the `exit 0`, so there is no conflict. I added no new decision block, since a comment isn't a decision.

**4. `bash -n scripts/check.sh`**
It printed nothing and exited with status 0, so the syntax is valid. `git status` shows only `scripts/check.sh` modified.
